english_translation: The first day at a new job is always intimidating for many people, but if you are brave and speak kindly with others, you quickly get used to the place in no time.

dialogue.shona: Zuva rekutanga kubasa idzva, rinogara richityisa kune vanhu vazhinji; asi kana ukashinga, uye uchitaura nevamwe zvakanaka, unokurumidza kujaira nzvimbo yacho pasina nguva.
dialogue.english: The first day at a new job is always intimidating for many people, but if you are brave and speak kindly with others, you quickly get used to the place in no time.
dialogue.literal_gloss: Zuva [sun / day] • rekutanga [rekutanga] • kubasa [to/at work] • idzva [idzva] • rinogara [it gara] • richityisa [richityisa] • kune [to / at ne] • vanhu [people] • vazhinji [people zhinji] • asi [but / however] • kana [if / when / or] • ukashinga [ukashinga] • uye [and / furthermore] • uchitaura [uchitaura] • nevamwe [and / with vamwe] • zvakanaka [well / nicely / very good] • unokurumidza [you kurumidza] • kujaira [to / at jaira]

grammar_notes.title: Talking About the Past ('zvakanaka')
grammar_notes.content: The verb 'zvakanaka' expresses a completed past action. Shona has two main ways to talk about the past: 1) For actions that happened earlier today or very recently, combine the short subject prefix ('nda-' = I, 'wa-' = you, 'a-' = he/she, 'ta-' = we, 'va-' = they) directly with the verb stem (e.g., 'ndamuka' = 'I woke up today', 'wabudirira' = 'you have succeeded'). 2) For events that happened yesterday or further in the past, insert '-ka-' after the subject prefix (e.g., 'takatenga' = 'we bought', 'vakaenda' = 'they went', 'akadanidzira' = 'he shouted').
grammar_notes.rule: Recent Today Past: [nda- / wa- / ta- / va-] + verb | Earlier Past: [ndaka- / waka- / taka- / vaka-] + verb

grammar_notes.title: Present Tense & Everyday Actions ('rinogara')
grammar_notes.content: The verb 'rinogara' uses the present marker '-no-'. In Shona, inserting '-no-' between the subject prefix and the verb stem expresses general truths, everyday habits, or states of mind like 'wanting', 'thinking', and 'knowing'. For example: 'ndinoda' ('I want/like'), 'unofunga' ('you think'), 'vanoti' ('they say'), and 'vanorima' ('they farm').
grammar_notes.rule: [ndi- (I) / u- (you) / a- (he/she) / ti- (we) / va- (they)] + -no- + verb -> Ndinoda (I want), Vanogara (They live)

grammar_notes.title: Talking About Location: 'pa-', 'ku-', and 'mu-' ('kubasa')
grammar_notes.content:
Look at how location is expressed with 'kubasa'. Instead of separate prepositions like 'on', 'to', or 'in', Shona attaches one of three location prefixes directly to the front of a noun:
• 'pa-' means 'at' or 'on' a specific point or surface (e.g., 'patafura' = on the table, 'pamusika' = at the market, 'pasi' = on the ground).
• 'ku-' means 'to', 'from', or 'at' a general destination (e.g., 'kuchikoro' = to school, 'kumusha' = to the rural home, 'kubasa' = at/to work).
• 'mu-' means 'inside' an enclosed space (e.g., 'mumba' = inside the house, 'muguta' = in the city, 'mumugwagwa' = in the road).
grammar_notes.rule: pa- = on / at a point (patafura) | ku- = to / at a place (kuchikoro) | mu- = inside (mumba)

cultural_notes.title: Starting a New Job ('Zuva Rekutanga kuBasa Idzva') & Building Workplace Rapport
cultural_notes.content: In Zimbabwean workplaces, courage ('kushinga') and speaking respectfully and warmly with colleagues ('kutaura nevamwe zvakanaka') are recognized as the quickest way to feel at home in a new environment.

active_exercises.prompt: Translate this new sentence into English: 'Ndasiya nharembozha yangu pachigaro mumba yokutandarira.'
options: Please close the door and all the windows before sleeping.
I left my mobile phone on the chair in the living room.
My keys are inside the small bag on the table.
We are sitting under the shade tree outside the house.
active_exercises.correct_answer: I left my mobile phone on the chair in the living room.
active_exercises.explanation: 'Ndasiya' = 'I left', 'nharembozha yangu' = 'my mobile phone', 'pachigaro' = 'on the chair', 'mumba yokutandarira' = 'in the living room'.

active_exercises.prompt: Choose the right locative prefix: You want to say 'The keys are ON the table' ('______tafura').
active_exercises.explanation: The prefix 'pa-' means 'on / at a specific surface', so 'pa-' + 'tafura' = 'patafura' ('on the table').

active_exercises.prompt: Translate this new sentence into English: 'Vanhu vakamira pamusika vachimirira kukwira bhazi.'
options: The driver stopped the car near the traffic lights.
We saw two large trucks carrying maize to the city.
The road to the eastern highlands has many curves.
People are standing at the market waiting to board the bus.
active_exercises.correct_answer: People are standing at the market waiting to board the bus.
active_exercises.explanation: 'Vanhu vakamira pamusika' = 'People are standing at the market', 'vachimirira kukwira bhazi' = 'waiting to board the bus'.
